what: DEFINITIVE source-protection TLDR for aide-memory binary migration, sourced from Bun's own docs (https://bun.com/docs/bundler/bytecode): (1) Bun's `--bytecode` flag is a startup performance optimization, NOT a source protection mechanism — Bun's docs explicitly state "It doesn't obscure source code" and "The .jsc file is useless without its corresponding .js file" (the .js source ships alongside the .jsc cache). Any blog/TLDR claiming --bytecode provides obfuscation-grade protection is factually wrong. (2) The only flags that actually protect: `--minify` (mangles identifiers, strips whitespace/comments) and excluding source maps. (3) Minified npm (esbuild --minify, no source maps, `package.json` files allowlist, CI check grepping tarball for .ts/.map/sourceMappingURL/src/) and Bun compile --minify provide ESSENTIALLY EQUIVALENT source protection — both produce bundled+minified+transpiled JS extractable in ~1-3 minutes via `unbuned`/`bun-decompile`/cat. (4) Both prevent the Claude Code 2026-03-31 "forkable public repo" scenario equally well. Neither protects against a motivated reverse-engineer with LLM-assisted deobfuscation (humanify, webcrack, CASCADE reach 0.79 execution-correctness on minified JS at ~$0.01-0.50 per sample). (5) Only genuine step-up from either JS approach: rewrite sensitive logic in Rust via napi-rs, ship compiled .node binary via npm optionalDependencies (Sentry/esbuild/swc/Turbo/Biome/Rspack/Rolldown/lightningcss pattern). Raises RE cost to days-weeks. (6) For aide-memory: the real open threat is accidental source map / raw source shipping (memory 142) — not the binary format. Most of the binary migration's operational cost (~2-3 weeks + signing + AV handling + cross-platform matrix) buys only ~2 minutes of extra reverse-engineering friction over minified npm. Honest recommendation stays Bun + shim IF there are non-protection reasons to want a binary (zero-Node UX, binary "real app" feel). Otherwise minified npm ships the protection goal at ~1 day cost.
why: User surfaced inconsistency in my framing + a pasted TLDR that incorrectly claimed --bytecode provides hours-days of reverse-engineering friction. Bun's own docs settle it: --bytecode is perf-only, doesn't obscure source. This is the definitive framing future spawns should use — sourced from the authoritative primary source, not third-party blog speculation.
